observation_summary: The regularized Gamma function returned values with insufficient precision, causing unit test assertions to fail due to small differences between expected and actual results.
reasoning_summary: The bug was caused by an overly loose numerical tolerance (epsilon) defined as a constant in the Gamma class. The value 10e-9 was insufficient for double-precision floating-point calculations, leading to precision loss in the regularized Gamma function. The fix involved tightening this constant to 10e-15, which aligns with standard double-precision expectations and resolves the discrepancy observed in the unit tests.
